To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we present a fast, reproducable and cheap method for simultaneously estimating the complete energetic budget of insects.
we provide a fast and reproducible method for simultaneously estimating the complete energetic budget of insects.
we present an easy and cheap method to simultaneously measure all the major energetic compartments (i.e. proteins, lipids, glycogen and free sugars) in the same insect individual.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of a new, fast, reliable and cheap method for simultaneously quantifying the four major energetic compartments in insects, and thus for studying the acquisition, storage and use of nutrients in a single individual, and for comparing individuals among species, populations and life-stages.
the validation of a method that should largely improve our knowledge on nutrient acquisition and allocation in insects.

the development of a simple, reproducible, cheap and fast protocol for simultaneously estimating four energetic components in the same individual insect, and we believe that it will be useful for a wide variety of insect ecologists, physiologists and evolutionary biologists.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the method presented in this study is a valuable alternative to the classical, partial methods for estimating energetic compartments.
our method provides a reliable tool for studying the complete energetic budget of insects.
this new method allows the simultaneous estimation of all the energetic compartments in insects with high sensitivity and reproducibility.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
this method is an important tool for the ecologist, physiologist and evolutionary biologist who wish to investigate the energetic budget in insects.

our method is a valuable tool to study nutrient acquisition and allocation, as well as to investigate the relationships between energetic reserves and life-history traits, in a wide range of insect species.

this method is an efficient, fast and inexpensive way to estimate the four energetic compartments in a same individual, and thus to assess the energy balance in insects.
